attribution.note: Marcus's own commentary in his Substack post, written in reply to Hinton's quote. It is not a quotation of someone else.

semantics.note: The statement has two parts: a claim that this has already happened, plus a firm 'will see a lot more' with no deadline. The normalised proposition keeps both parts and the open-ended time frame.

contract.note: The plain reading of 'we will see a lot more [cases]' is real-world manipulation incidents piling up over time. The contract instead lets one controlled study, using manipulative messages written by researchers, count as 'a lot more.' That stretches the claim in the speaker's favour. The contract's own ambiguity flags admit that an everyday-incident reading would need more evidence.

evidence.note: A 2020 PNAS experiment in which AI adversaries steered real participants' choices. It weakly supports the 'already seen cases' part, but in lab tasks only. It says nothing about the forecast.

A 2025 HBS preprint: in a controlled experiment, scripted manipulative farewells increased how long people kept engaging. This shows the effect can be produced in a lab. It does not show real-world cases accumulating, which is what the fair reading requires.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. On a fair plain reading, 'a lot more' cases means real-world manipulation incidents growing over time. The packet has only lab experiments, and its stated gaps say real-world incidence and its change since 2023 are not established. Counting experimental participants as cases, as the contract does, stretches the claim in the speaker's favour, so no conclusive event is met. Unresolved.
